does: Rolls seasoned minced meat between wet palms into round balls of an even size, so that they hold together and cook at the same pace.
how: Knead the minced meat with its seasoning until it holds together, and chill it briefly so that it handles well.
Wet the hands, or rub them with a little oil, so that the meat does not stick.
Take up equal portions with a spoon, to keep the balls the same size.
Roll each portion between the palms with light pressure until it is round and smooth, with no cracks.
Set the balls on a tray, not touching, until they are cooked.

cues.text: The balls are the same size, smooth and round, with no cracks.
Each ball holds together when it is lifted, and springs back a little under a finger.

mistakes.mistake: Packing the balls hard, which makes them dense and dry.
mistakes.fix: Roll with light pressure, only until they hold.

mistakes.mistake: Making balls of different sizes, so that some are done before others.
mistakes.fix: Portion the meat with a spoon before rolling.

mistakes.mistake: Working with dry hands, so that the meat sticks and tears.
mistakes.fix: Wet or oil the hands often.

comes_after.why: Minced meat is kneaded with its seasoning so that it holds together before it is rolled.

variant_of.differs: Shape forms a soft mixture into even pieces between spoons. Here the meat is firm enough to be rolled by hand into round balls, and the mixture must first be kneaded to bind.
